author: WHOLESOMEest Boi
body:
Below is the deck-by-deck layout of where everything is tucked inside that 40-meter frame.

Upper Deck: The Command & Special Ops Hub
The upper deck is the "dry" side of the ship, focused on mission control and the transport of high-value "cargo."

Cockpit (Forward Nose): Located at the very tip of the wedge. It features a tight 3–4 station setup for the pilot, gunner, and systems op. The neural-link chairs have cracked haptic feedback and the wraparound holoscreens are prone to static.

Armory / Ready Room (Directly behind Cockpit): The staging area for missions. It contains lockers for vac-suits and small arms, fold-down briefing benches, and a central holo-table for asteroid mapping.

The Nursery (Port Mid-Section): A converted, sealed storage locker repurposed for children. It holds 3–4 foldable cribs with restraint webbing for high-G maneuvers, soft-glow monitors, and auto-feeders that dispense nutrient paste laced with trace calmatives.

Pleasure Pod (Starboard Mid-Section): An aftermarket modular unit for "relief". It includes a zero-G chamber with adaptive haptic walls and a seated VR rig with scent/heat options. Access is controlled by a coin-slot timer, though the crew frequently hacks the override.

Lower Deck: The Guts & Grime
The lower deck is where the crew survives. It is louder, hotter, and smells of recycled air and ozone.

Crew Living Area & Gym (Central Midsection): A multipurpose space with a compact gravity ring (adjustable 0.5–1.5g) to prevent muscle atrophy. It features resistance bands, a punch-bag made of salvaged padding, and ratty acceleration couches that double as seating for a communal table.

Galley & Mess (Aft of Living Area): Contains one auto-chef and a hot-plate. The water recycler here uses a "flavor boost" additive to mask the metallic taste of reclaimed water.

author: WHOLESOMEest Boi
body:
Bunks (Lower Mid-Aft): Two stacked pods containing 5–6 bunks each. Space is so tight that "hot-bunking" (sharing bunks across shifts) is common. Personal lockers have biometric locks that frequently glitch.

Engineering & Cargo Access (Stern/Belly): Tight crawlspaces lead to the overclocked fusion bottle. The small cargo bay has tie-downs for sample crates and a belly airlock for rapid drops. Hidden floor compartments under the gym and engineering are used for contraband and extra ammo.

System Quirks & Atmosphere
Sensory Profile: Harsh white lighting in the armory contrasts with the dim red of the bunks and pulsing neon in the pleasure pod. You'll hear a high-pitched whine during maneuvers and the occasional muffled thump from the gym.

Life Support: Strictly metered on per-person timers. Gravity plates are only located in the living/gym area; the rest of the ship remains in zero-G to save weight and power.

Stealth & Defense: The ship features a "low-observability" mode where thrusters are kept cold and only passive sensors are used. For combat, it relies on a fixed spinal cannon and four turreted machine guns for suppression.

This ship is effectively a "sports car with guns". It’s built to burn in, drop a team (and perhaps their families in the nursery), and burn out before anyone can lock on.

author: WHOLESOMEest Boi
body:
Galley & Mess (Forward Mid-Section)
Layout & Atmosphere:
The galley is positioned just forward of the ladder well, creating a natural buffer between the high-traffic corridor and the ship’s living quarters. The space is compact but efficiently arranged, with warm recessed lighting that mimics the glow of a hearth. The walls are lined with magnetic knife strips and retractable prep surfaces, while the ceiling has a series of small, articulated herb planters under grow lamps. The air smells faintly of roasted spices and ozone from the 3D printers.

Key Features:

Auto-Chef "Culinator 9000":

Functionality: A multi-purpose unit that combines molecular gastronomy, 3D food printing, and traditional cooking methods. It can synthesize proteins from base nutrients, but its real strength is layering flavors and textures to mimic home-cooked meals.
Menu Options: Pre-loaded with a diverse recipe database—from spicy stir-fries to hearty stews—plus a "custom" mode where crew can input flavor profiles or even scan a dish for replication.
Output: Produces meals with realistic textures (e.g., crispy skin on synth-chicken, al dente pasta) rather than uniform paste. The printer nozzle can extrude intricate shapes for garnishes or desserts.
Hot-Plate & Grill Surface:

A retractable induction hot-plate with a built-in grill grate for searing or charring. Useful for finishing 3D-printed steaks or toasting flatbreads. The surface self-sanitizes with plasma arcs between uses.
Communal Table:

author: WHOLESOMEest Boi
body:
A scarred metal table bolted to the deck, with deep scratches from knife work and faint burns from past cooking experiments. The edges are rounded from years of crew leaning against it. A small recess in the center holds a communal salt/pepper dispenser and a bottle of hot sauce.
Water Recycler with "Flavor Boost":

The recycler filters wastewater into potable water, but the "flavor boost" adds a mild euphoric additive—think a faint, pleasant buzz like a light kombucha. The flavor profile rotates daily (e.g., citrus-mint, ginger-lemongrass) to keep it interesting.
Secondary Briefing Area:

A wall-mounted holo-screen dominates one bulkhead, retracting into the ceiling when not in use. The table doubles as a briefing surface, with holographic overlays for tactical discussions. The crew often eats while reviewing mission plans.
3D Printers & Food Tech:

Protein Synthesizer: Converts base nutrients (e.g., algae, insect protein) into customizable meat analogs. Can print anything from fish fillets to ribs.
Spice/Herb Printer: Grows and prints fresh herbs (basil, cilantro, mint) and spice blends on demand.
Dessert Module: Specializes in intricate sweets—chocolate sculptures, layered mousses, or nutrient-dense energy bites.
Crew Interaction:
The galley is the social hub of the ship. Crew members linger here long after meals, tweaking recipes on the auto-chef or experimenting with the 3D printers. The scarred table bears witness to late-night card games, heated debates, and the occasional "flavor boost"-fueled storytelling session.

Maintenance Notes:

The auto-chef requires regular calibration to avoid texture glitches (e.g., soggy synth-bread).
The water recycler’s euphoric additive is monitored to prevent overindulgence.
The herb planters need weekly trimming to avoid overgrowth into the walkway.
